reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports the key premises: E1 establishes laser cladding as a suitable method for TC4, and E2 demonstrates that Ni addition in a laser-cladded TiAl-based coating leads to solid solution strengthening and a hardness of 627.5 HV0.2, far exceeding typical TC4 hardness. The premises are accurately represented, though the specific Ni range (5-10 at.%) and carbide formation are not explicitly detailed in the cited passages.
premises: Laser cladding can produce high-quality, well-bonded coatings on TC4 with low porosity and dense structures.
Adding Ni to a TiAl-based coating can induce solid solution strengthening and alter phase composition.
Ni addition promotes solid solution diffusion into phases like Ti(Al,Cu)2, increasing lattice stress and hindering dislocations.
A laser-cladded coating with increased Ni content can achieve significantly higher hardness than the TC4 substrate.
A transition zone with intermediate hardness forms between the coating and substrate, buffering stresses.
